steps.title: Open the Desk page
steps.narration: This page scans about a hundred well-known stocks and shows which ones sit closest to one of their own key price levels today. It also keeps a record of every past scan.
steps.point_out: Today's ranked list, the stocks it had to skip, and the full history of past scans.

steps.title: Look at a past scan
steps.narration: You can open any earlier scan and see it exactly as it was recorded that day.
steps.point_out: A banner makes clear you're looking at an older scan, not today's, plus an honest note on the stocks that had no price history to rank that day.

expect.text: Viewing the recorded screen for 2026-06-22 — not the latest.

steps.title: Jump from a ranked stock straight into its chart
steps.narration: Clicking anywhere on a ranked stock's row takes you straight to its price chart, already loaded for that exact day.
steps.point_out: The chart opens pre-filled with the stock and date, showing its key price level.

steps.title: Move to the live tape reader
steps.narration: The Desk sits alongside two earlier pages, both reachable from the same menu at the top.
steps.point_out: The Cockpit page opens, ready to watch a stock's price action.

steps.title: Name a practice stock
steps.narration: Typing in a practice ticker that always settles into a predictable pattern, so you can try the reader without needing a real market feed.
steps.point_out: The ticker field now reads SIM-BUYER.

steps.title: Watch the tape settle
steps.narration: After watching for a moment, the reading settles into a clear call.
steps.point_out: The Tape State panel shows the bold read-out "Buyer Control", with live price bars, trades, and an event log all filled in.

steps.title: Switch to a real recorded stock
steps.narration: Switching to Historical mode replays a real stock's own recorded price action instead of a live practice feed.
steps.point_out: The Historical option is now selected.

steps.title: Name the real stock
steps.narration: Typing in a real stock symbol to replay its recorded price history.
steps.point_out: The symbol field now reads AAPL.

steps.title: Choose the day to replay
steps.narration: Typing in the day to replay.

steps.title: Fill the trading day in one click
steps.narration: One click fills in the whole trading day, instead of typing exact times by hand.
steps.point_out: The start and end time fields fill in automatically.

steps.title: Start the replay
steps.narration: Watching starts the replay of that real stock's real trading day.
steps.point_out: The page now shows it is watching AAPL.

steps.title: See the real chart with its key levels drawn on
steps.narration: Switching the chart to hourly bars shows the stock's real recorded price history, with its key support and resistance levels drawn right on top.
steps.point_out: Real candles, the timeframe switch, and the price-level lines are all drawn on the same chart.

expect.text: Recorded 1h bars sit left of the start marker; bars to its right are built live from the tape.

steps.title: Open the price-level map fresh
steps.narration: The Structure page maps a chosen stock's key support and resistance levels over its real price history.
steps.point_out: A report panel plainly says whether it has been worked out yet for this page — never a blank or made-up result.

steps.title: Choose a stock to map
steps.narration: Typing in a stock to load its price levels.
steps.point_out: The Symbol field now reads AAPL.

steps.title: Choose the date to look at
steps.narration: Typing in the exact date and time to look at.
steps.point_out: The As-of field now reads the chosen date and time.

steps.title: Load its key price levels
steps.narration: Loading draws the stock's real price history with its key support and resistance levels marked on top.
steps.point_out: The level table and the chart both show a level around 300.11, a well-known price wall for this stock.

steps.title: Study one past price touch
steps.narration: Clicking a past case opens a closer look at how the price behaved when it touched that level.
steps.point_out: A drill-in panel opens showing how the price reacted, its returns afterward, and the recorded trades around it, or an honest note if none were recorded.
